formula: observed ~ uvb + offset(log(expected)) + (1 | region)
notes: UK malignant-melanoma mortality vs UVB (Langford, Bentham & McDonald 1998). 70 counties nested in 11 regions; observed the death count, expected the offset, county one row each (ignored). Hand sample #11: the formula is a proposed UK-only restriction; the paper's Model A is a European three-level Poisson model with nation and region intercepts and a dispersion parameter, and no source located documents this UK-only fit.

formula: target ~ Scorer_1 + Scorer_2 + (1|Subject)
notes: analcatdata apnea1 (Simonoff 2003): target holds contingency-table cell frequencies for pairs of two scorers' nominal classifications (Scorer_1, Scorer_2) within 19 subjects, 25 cells each. Hand sample #11: the random intercept on Subject is proposed; PMLB does not state it and Simonoff's loglinear specification was not located.

formula: log(P(abuse=k)/P(abuse=1)) = beta_0k + beta_age,k*age + beta_temp,k*temp + beta_Paymed,k*Paymed + beta_Selfmed,k*Selfmed + beta_Wrdiag,k*Wrdiag + u_hosp,k + v_doc,k, k=2,3
notes: Antibiotic prescriptions within doctors within hospitals. Hand sample #11: Skrondal & Rabe-Hesketh's GLLAMM article, Table 3: a nominal logit with category-specific coefficients, category 1 the base, and correlated category-specific intercepts at the doctor and hospital levels; Table 4 adds DRed and WHO. abuse holds the levels 1-3 as floats, which could be ordered, so it stays ordinal; the fitted model is nominal, not proportional odds. RULE GAP: the documented nominal logit has no registry family value.

formula: relatt ~ eduminmin + income + unemployed + female + single + divorced + widowed + loglocurb + gini + edumin.ave + unempl.ave + div.ave + (1|country)
notes: Snijders & Bosker (2012) ch. 17: religious attendance of individuals in countries, a binary logit. Hand sample #11: the authors' ch17.r, Table 17.2. eduminmin is edlevel minus its country mean, edumin.ave the country mean of edlevel minus 17, unempl.ave and div.ave country means of unemployed and divorced: no column of the sheet, so they stay in the formula only and the covariates name the raw columns. gini centred at 35, loglocurb at 10; Turkey removed and income capped at 3. relpar, religiousregulation, tertiaryschoolenrollment and urbanization are not in this fit. Table 17.3 adds country random slopes for income and eduminmin.

formula: sqrt(CD4PCT) ~ time + (1 + time || newpid), time = visage - baseage
documented_prior: mu_a1 ~ normal(0, 1); a1 ~ normal(10*mu_a1, sigma_a1); mu_a2 ~ normal(0, 1); a2 ~ normal(0.1*mu_a2, sigma_a2); beta ~ normal(0, 1)
notes: Raw HIV CD4 data; ARM's script fits hiv.stan with response sqrt(CD4PCT), time = visage - baseage named once as visage, and the patient id remapped from newpid; intercepts and slopes independent, so ||. Fitted on treatmnt == 1, 1 < baseage < 5 and nonmissing CD4PCT: 369 rows on 83 children after excluding missing time. CD4CNT alternate response, VDATE date and VISIT id ignored; arv and baseage retained. hiv_inter.stan is fitted only on simulated data. Hand sample #11: the script states the intended model but has indexing and setup inconsistencies, among them a hard-coded J = 84, so it is no clean reproducible fit.

formula: yield ~ (1|gen) + (1|env)
notes: Multi-environment potato trial (Tai 1971); yield is the mean of a 4-rep RCB at each environment, 48 genotype-environment cell means. variety is the genotype name (duplicate of gen); loc and year are the components of env; all ignored. Hand sample #11: the help gives a dotplot and a stability-analysis stub, not this crossed random-intercept model, which is proposed; Tai's stability analysis is not equivalent to it.

formula: logit(p_ij) = beta0 + betaR*respisrr_ij + betaT*tel_ij + betaM*mail_ij + betaY*year_j + betaS*saliency_j + betaTY*tel_ij*year_j + betaMY*mail_ij*year_j + u0_j + uT_j*tel_ij + uM_j*mail_ij; j = source; response a proportion, binomial with denominator denom
notes: Survey response rates of data-collection modes (face-to-face, telephone, mail) nested within studies (source). Hand sample #11: Hox's chapter 6, Eq. 6.21 and Table 6.5, final model: binomial logit on the proportion response with denominator denom, face-to-face the reference, a study intercept and telephone and mail random slopes; the equation lists no random-effect covariances. respisrr distinguishes response from completion rate; year coded from 1947. response holds proportions, so it is filed continuous and denom stays in ignore; integer successes are not derived from rounded proportions. RULE GAP: the documented binomial family has no registry value. Distinct from the chapter 11 multivariate analysis.

formula: rt_raw ~ spkr * prec * load + (1 | subj) + (1 + prec | item)
notes: Kronmueller & Barr 2007, subj x item crossed, full 2x2x2 factorial. rt_trunc is the truncated-RT alternate response, ignored. Hand sample #11: the model is fitted in the MixedModels.jl v3.7 rank-deficiency example, not the formula_syntax page; the OSF download (version 9) is a gzip tar archive containing kb07.arrow.

formula: conc ~ SSbiexp(Time, A1, lrc1, A2, lrc2) + (A1 + lrc1 + A2 + lrc2|Subject)
notes: NONLINEAR: biexponential pharmacokinetics (Pinheiro and Bates 2000 App. A.4). Hand sample #11: Cefamandole.Rd fits nlsList(SSbiexp, data = Cefamandole), separate subject-wise nonlinear least-squares curves conc ~ SSbiexp(Time, A1, lrc1, A2, lrc2) | Subject: the mean function is documented, the random effects on all four parameters are proposed. The formula is a pseudo-lme4 rendering, not lme4 syntax.

formula: RT ~ 1 + Correct + Trial + PrevType * meanWeight + Frequency + NativeLanguage * Length + (1|Subject) + (1|Word)
notes: lmer; worked example of the help (Baayen 2008, Analyzing Linguistic Data). Random-slope variants in the help keep the same grouping factors; meanRT is the by-item mean response; other by-item aggregates (SubjFreq, meanSize) and unused lexical columns remain usable. Hand sample #11: RT is already a log reaction time; it is not logged again.

formula: conc ~ biexponential(Time; Formulation effect; random effects on Subject)
notes: NONLINEAR: 40 concentrations on five subjects; same design as Tetracycline1 with different formulations and subjects, not a copy. Hand sample #11: neither the help nor the package code states a model: groupedData metadata conc ~ Time | Subject with inner Formulation only. The biexponential mean and the random parameters are proposed.

formula: POS ~ TREAT * TIME + (TIME | ID)
notes: Ch.5 (UCLA R page) Model A: lme(pos ~ treat*time, random=~time|id). Positive mood over days; TIME333/TIME667 are recentered time axes used in models B/C.

formula: kicks ~ 0 + (1 | corps) + (1 | year), both sd fixed at 0.5, no intercept, year as a category
notes: von Bortkiewicz Prussian horse-kick deaths: kicks per corps per year (14 corps x 20 years), a count panel. man/PrussianHorses.Rd:30-42 fits m0: kicks ~ poisson(lambda), log(lambda) = d[corps] + y[year], d and y each normal(0, 0.5), no overall intercept, year a category. Hand sample #11: the fixed scales are priors, not estimated variance components.

formula: cum ~ ult*(1-exp(-(dev/theta)^omega)); ult ~ 1+(1|AY); omega ~ 1; theta ~ 1; Gaussian, nl=TRUE
documented_prior: c(prior(normal(5000, 1000), nlpar = "ult"), prior(normal(1, 2), nlpar = "omega"), prior(normal(45, 10), nlpar = "theta"))
notes: NONLINEAR: brms help example fit_loss (Gaussian nonlinear; Gesmann & Morris 2020, hierarchical compartmental reserving). Cumulative loss cum grows with development month dev. premium is an unused usable column. Confidence capped at medium by the nonlinear rule. Hand sample #11: theta and omega are estimated population-level nonlinear parameters with normal priors, not fixed constants; ult has an origin-year varying intercept.

formula: r ~ I + m + b + m:b + I:v + I:t + I:f + I:m + I:b + I:v:t + I:v:b + (1|sid)
notes: ROS Incentives survey-nonresponse meta-analysis: 101 conditions in 39 studies (sid), r the response rate. basen and the derived difference columns ignored. Hand sample #11: Gelman, Stevens & Chan (2003), preferred Model III, Table 2 and Eq. 5, linked by the ROS README: a Gaussian identity-link approximation on the rates, residual variance sigma^2 + r_i(1 - r_i)/basen_i, a study intercept with variance tau^2. v, t and f are zero without incentives, so I:v = v, I:t = t, I:f = f, I:v:t = v:t and I:v:b = v:b. basen sets the known sampling variance, not binomial trials.

formula: cbind(awards, applications - awards) ~ gender + (1 | discipline)
notes: McElreath ch. 11 practice: Dutch NWO grant awards out of applications per discipline x gender (18 rows). Hand sample #11: the exercise is a binomial GLM with discipline as a fixed adjustment; no hierarchical discipline intercept is fitted in the pinned package, so the (1 | discipline) model is proposed.

formula: rentsqm = beta0 + f1(area) + f2(yearc) + fgeo(district) + beta1*glocation + beta2*tlocation + epsilon; epsilon Gaussian
notes: Munich 1999 rent survey; rent is the alternate response. Hand sample #11: Fahrmeir, Kneib, Lang & Marx (2013), Example 9.2, Eq. 9.8: smooth effects of area and yearc, a district spatial effect by kriging at the district centroids (a structured covariance, so district stays the grouping factor), glocation and tlocation the good and top indicators derived from location. bath, kitchen and cheating are not in this model; Eq. 9.7 also omits the location indicators.

formula: delta ~ Group + Temperature + Type + Thick + (1 | uWafer)
notes: uWafer is the unique group/temperature/type/wafer id (grouping); Site is the within-wafer replicate and Wafer a component of uWafer, both ignored; Thick is a covariate (spot check #22). Group, Temperature and Type are between-wafer factors. Littell Data Set 5.8. Hand sample #11: the help only calls str and the object's groupedData metadata gives delta ~ 1 | uWafer; neither states the fixed effects or the full random structure of Littell's strip-plot ANCOVA, so the model is proposed. Temperature is an unordered factor in the pinned RDA, though the help calls it ordered.

formula: read ~ occasion + occasion2 + (1+occasion|id)
notes: Curran longitudinal data, children over occasions; anti (antisocial behaviour) is the alternate response. Hand sample #11: Hox's PanelModeling chapter, Table x.1, second model: reading recognition growth with linear and quadratic occasion and a correlated subject intercept and linear slope, other covariates omitted for exposition. The earlier six-predictor antisocial model was not found in an author source.

formula: Y ~ LRT + I(LRT^2) + VR_1 + VR_2 + Gender + School_gender_1 + School_gender_2 + School_denom_1 + School_denom_2 + School_denom_3 + (1+LRT+VR_1|school); residual variance = exp(-(theta+phi*LRT))
documented_prior: beta ~ normal(0, 100); theta ~ normal(0, 100); phi ~ normal(0, 100); gamma ~ multi_normal(gamma_mu, gamma_Sigma); Sigma ~ inv_wishart(3, invR)
notes: schools.stan: per-school random intercept and slopes on LRT and VR_1 (alpha ~ multi_normal(gamma, Sigma)), 38 schools, 1978 pupils; Y a standardised exam score. Hand sample #11: the formula keeps the LRT^2 term and the heteroscedastic residual variance of schools.stan; LRT is filed once as a covariate per the polynomial rule.

formula: I(y > 0) ~ anger + gender + do_want + other_self + blame + express + (1|person)
notes: Verbal-aggression items (De Boeck & Wilson): y takes 0/1/2 (no, perhaps, yes) over 24 items crossed with persons; i1-i24 are the item dummies (ignored). Hand sample #11: MLMUS4 chapter 10, exercise 10.4, step 3: y recoded to 1 for perhaps or yes, then a person-intercept logistic model with these six predictors, no item intercept. The response names its raw ordinal column, the recode in the formula. RULE GAP: the documented Bernoulli logit on the recode has no registry family value.

formula: log(estrmeas) ~ 1 + (1 | subject)
notes: Five women, 16 independent estrone assays each, no temporal order; estrone.sav is the wide twin. Hand sample #11: Hox's DataStories says the assays are log-transformed before the chapter 13 estimation example, but no source located gives the empty-model specification, so it is proposed. log_estr is log10(estrmeas), not the natural log of the narrative; the base is left unresolved.

formula: AvgDailyGain ~ 1 + (1|Sire/Dam)
notes: Five sires, two dams within each sire, two progeny each; dam codes are reused within sire. The page says it appears to be a constructed data set, which is no statement of simulation, so it stays. Hand sample #11: Animal.Rd only calls str and the object's metadata gives AvgDailyGain ~ 1 | Sire/Dam; no inspected help or vignette fits the nested variance-components model, so it is proposed.

formula: y ~ treat + v4 + lage + lbas + lbas_trt + (1|subj)
notes: Thall-Vail progabide epilepsy trial, seizure counts y over 4 visits per subject; cons a constant. Hand sample #11: the authors' SABRE exercises 13.3, steps 3-4: a subject-intercept Poisson model; step 3 uses visit, step 4 replaces it with v4, so visit leaves the model. lbas_trt is the precomputed centred log-baseline by treatment interaction, not the product of the displayed lbas and treat columns, so it is a covariate.

formula: TICKS ~ YEAR + HEIGHT + (1|BROOD) + (1|INDEX) + (1|LOCATION)
notes: Help example full_mod1 (Poisson glmer, Elston et al. 2001). INDEX is the observation-level random effect (one row per level): it stays in the formula and in ignore, not in grouping_factors (#20); cHEIGHT is the centred HEIGHT, ignored. Hand sample #11: the documented model has the INDEX term for overdispersion; YEAR is a factor in the RDA.
